title: Epigame participant state
description: What a player is told about their own game, carried as the `state` of a participant state document. Points are a pure function of state the participant was already shown, so the app can compute the same answer for immediate feedback; the server's copy is authoritative because the cost of protection is what the study measures, and a cost the client can edit is not a cost. Deliberately small -- a player sees their own situation and one aggregate, not the study's data.

day.description: Which day of the game the last tick covered. Zero before the first tick has run.

days_total.description: How long the game lasts, so the app can show progress without reading the bundle again. Null for a study that declares no schedule and therefore has no last day. Required but nullable rather than optional: 'this game does not end' is an answer the app has to render, and an absent field would be indistinguishable from a server that forgot.

epi_state.description: The participant's state in the twin. `dead` is defined so the contract does not have to widen later; the default SIR model never produces it.

points.description: Confirmed score. Signed, because a game whose costs can exceed its rewards should show that rather than clamping to zero and hiding it.

protected_until.description: When protection lapses, or null when unprotected. An instant rather than a boolean so the app can count down and expire it locally without waiting for the next tick.

protection_source.description: Why the participant is protected. The game treats a deliberate choice and a phone that stopped sensing identically, but research needs to tell them apart.

total_cases.description: Cumulative infections across the whole simulated population, including virtual participants. The one aggregate a player sees.

population.description: Size of the simulated population, so `total_cases` means something. Includes virtual participants, whose presence the information screen discloses.

pending_contacts.description: Scoring contacts detected since the last tick and not yet confirmed. Lets the app show that something is coming without keeping a second ledger.

settlement.description: How the last day's points were arrived at. Present so a participant can check the arithmetic rather than trust it, which is what makes a server-authoritative score acceptable. Null before the first day has been settled.

day.description: Which day this settles. Always the day before `day` once the game is running.

opening.description: Balance carried in, so `opening` plus the lines must equal `closing`.

closing.description: Balance carried out. Equal to the `points` a participant is shown.

lines.description: Every movement, including zero-valued ones. A day that earned nothing because the device was not sensing says so, rather than showing an unexplained gap.

reason.description: Why the balance moved. `not_sensing` is a withheld accrual rather than a charge: a day the study could not observe is not scored, but neither is it penalised. `carried_over` credits a contact whose other side arrived after its own day was settled, which is never rewritten.

points.description: Signed. Zero is meaningful and is not omitted.

count.description: How many contacts this line represents, where the reason is a contact one.
